purpose: Curated editorial themes for Digital Pulse (Type C). Unlike Liquid Pulse (D), which the substrate reader derives from ctDNA-capable biomarker records, Digital Pulse themes are NOT derivable from the substrate — they are external developments (a cleared algorithm, a validation study, a method) that we choose to cover. This file is the input the Type C branch of enumerate_thematic reads.

schema.theme: the editorial subject of one Digital Pulse article
schema.substrate_markers: marker/morphology names this theme grounds to, for cross-cancer linking (matched against ihc_signature / molecular_signature / biomarker fields in the substrate)
schema.cancers: which cancer substrates this theme touches
schema.status_hint: editorial seed only; the Research stage confirms current status at write time
schema.notes: curation note / why this is a Digital Pulse theme

policy: status_hint is an editorial seed, NOT a verified fact. The Type C Research prompt independently confirms regulatory status, dates, and validation evidence at write time. Refresh this list as the field moves; it is editorially maintained, not auto-generated. NCCN not used.

themes.theme: FDA-cleared multimodal AI prognostic tools in localized prostate cancer
themes.status_hint: first AI SaMD De Novo authorization in digital pathology reported 2025; verify identifier and indication at write time
themes.notes: Anchors the Digital Pulse 'computational prognostication' story; connects to the prostate grading-as-spine substrate. Ties directly to the Digital Pathology Today editorial world.

themes.theme: AI-based risk stratification entering HR+/HER2- early breast cancer
themes.status_hint: FDA clearance of a digital-pathology breast risk-stratification tool reported 2026; verify exact indication and date
themes.notes: Positions computational risk scoring alongside the existing multigene-assay substrate (Oncotype/MammaPrint). Strong reader interest: where does an image-based score sit relative to genomic assays?

themes.theme: Computational HER2 image analysis and the HER2-low/ultralow reproducibility problem
themes.status_hint: active validation literature through 2024-2025; mostly investigational/assistive, not autonomous; verify
themes.notes: Directly grounded in the HER2 substrate record and the ultralow reproducibility issue from the sample article. The diagnostic-problem framing (can image analysis make the 0-vs-ultralow call reproducible?) is the spine.

themes.theme: AI-assisted cancer detection as a screening/pre-screen layer in prostate and breast biopsies
themes.status_hint: first-of-kind CAD detection tools FDA-cleared since 2021; verify current scope
themes.notes: The 'AI surfaces high-risk regions before the pathologist opens the slide' workflow story. Connects to the diagnostic-IHC-triad substrate (prostate) and in-situ/invasive detection (breast).

themes.theme: Computational Ki-67 quantification: where image analysis helps and where it doesn't
themes.status_hint: assistive/quantitative; standardization remains the open problem; verify
themes.notes: A genuinely cross-cancer theme — Ki-67 appears in four substrates. The Digital Pulse angle is reproducibility and the International Ki-67 Working Group standardization gap.

themes.theme: FDA regulatory frameworks for AI/ML Software as a Medical Device in pathology
themes.status_hint: FDA draft/final guidance on AI-enabled devices issued 2025; verify
themes.notes: The meta-theme: how the clearance pathway itself works (De Novo, 510(k), lifecycle management). Grounds the whole Digital Pulse line and explains why so few tools are cleared. No specific marker — it's the regulatory backbone piece.
